newsitem.title: USA: US feedlot cattle market quiet, tone firm-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US feedlot cattle market quiet, tone firm-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. feedlot cattle markets were quiet near midday Thursday, with no reported sales but prices expected to be firm whenever cattle do sell again, amid strong packer demand, feedlot sources said.
Packer bids mostly at $67.00 per cwt were passed by owners asking $68.00 to $69.00, sources said.

Cattle Wednesday sold at a top of $67.00 in active sales, with about 300 head at $67.50, several sources said. A large part of the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma and Kansas showlists were sold. Cattle not sold were being held by owners anticipating $68.00 either Thursday or early next week.
